title: Clara Barton Founds a Red Cross Before Her Country Signs the Treaty
conflicts: Founding date 21 May 1881 (Barton's own book, Red Cross, NWHM, Dansville library) versus 'June 1881' (NPS handbook, i.e. the 9 June officers' meeting); story gives both meetings. Meeting place (Barton's I Street apartment versus Senator Conger's home) left unstated. Blaine's letter dated 20 May (both Barton books) versus 23 May (Moynier's reply); 20 May used. Hayes approach dated 1877 by Barton and 1878 by the NPS and Hayes's own note; no year given. Michigan relief: $80,000 (NPS) versus Dansville's $300 (Dansville library); no figure used.
notes: Strong primary material: Barton's own 1899 book and her cousin W. E. Barton's 1922 biography (both on Project Gutenberg), balanced by the 1981 National Park Service handbook by Elizabeth Brown Pryor, which notes Barton unfairly disparaged earlier advocates; the story does not claim she was the only advocate. Library of Congress pages returned 403 and were not used.
